experiments.name: Wikipedia attention lead
experiments.plain: Do Wikipedia attention surges on US stocks that have not moved yet come before big up moves that a buyer could use?
experiments.lesson: Page-view spikes hinted a big move was coming, but crashes as often as jumps; no extra return.
experiments.verdict: NO USABLE LEAD: 1,473 events, excess 20-session return +0.10% (t 0.24); surges precede big moves both ways.

experiments.name: Reproduction of Hermes's 3 November studies
experiments.plain: Do Hermes's 3 November entry, exit and bear-market conclusions hold when rebuilt from scratch on fresh Binance data?
experiments.lesson: Rebuilt another AI's studies from scratch: nearly all held, but 'winners show by day 3' was wrong.
experiments.verdict: Conclusions hold: 45 claims, 36 reproduced, 7 partly, 2 not ('winners show by day 3' is wrong).

experiments.name: Look-ahead corrections to NEIGHBOURS and PRESSURE

experiments.lesson: Fixed a bug that quietly used future information; both earlier 'no' answers still stood.
experiments.verdict: Both original verdicts CONFIRMED; the correction moved results only in the fourth decimal.

experiments.name: Peer coins and 'next stop'

must_contain: Neighbours add no information. Next stop adds no information.

experiments.verdict: No information: peers made the 3-day ranking slightly worse (-0.005); confirmed by the corrected run.

experiments.name: Taker-buy pressure

experiments.lesson: A day of heavy buying pointed slightly the wrong way; crowds arriving usually fade.
experiments.verdict: No incremental value; urgent buying points slightly the wrong way. Confirmed by the corrected run.

experiments.name: Stablecoin tide / alt seesaw
experiments.plain: Does stablecoin supply or the alts-versus-BTC seesaw at the start of a month predict next month's moonshots?
experiments.lesson: Money flow describes the crypto market but doesn't predict it; months it flagged as good were worse.

must_contain: Reading: FLOW DESCRIBES, DOES NOT LEAD.

experiments.verdict: FLOW DESCRIBES, DOES NOT LEAD: the locked 'tide on' rule was worse in the check period.

experiments.name: Group-backed US jumps
experiments.plain: Do US +30% jumps that happen together with their sector peers hold up better than lone jumps?
experiments.lesson: Passed on past data: backed jumps crashed half as often as lone ones, but still lost money.
experiments.verdict: FLOW-BACKED JUMPS LAST, but only as 'less bad', not a buy signal (lone jumps crash about twice as often).

experiments.name: When to buy a US +30% spike

experiments.lesson: None of 120 buy-timing rules was reliable; the best one lost money on a second period.

experiments.lesson: Executives' purchases did a bit better, but too few cases to tell it apart from luck.
experiments.verdict: FAIL (G1 t 1.21 < 1.65); closed per protocol, no rerun.

experiments.name: Lead ladder, international
experiments.plain: Do the pre-move features found in IDX replicate on other exchanges?
experiments.lesson: Earlier warning signs didn't repeat in nine other markets; they predict big moves, not direction.
experiments.verdict: NOT_REPLICATED.

experiments.name: IDX foreign/broker flow lead
experiments.plain: Does money flow in IDX stocks show up before their big up moves?
experiments.lesson: Foreign and big-buyer activity didn't show up before big rises; 0 of 256 checks passed.
experiments.verdict: NO_FLOW_LEAD: 0 of 256 gated cells pass.

experiments.name: E1: IDX moonshot detector (D1)
experiments.plain: Can a detector spot IDX stocks starting a big repricing, and does buying them make money?
experiments.lesson: Spotted jumps under way, but caught only 1 in 10 in time; buying lost 4% a trade.

must_contain: the obvious way to act on it loses
money. The paper policy therefore passes on D1 candidates

experiments.verdict: D1 sees repricings better than chance, but acting on it loses money; paper policy PASSes (no buy). Part of the closed early-entry record.

experiments.name: E2: US and crypto big-up-day detectors
experiments.plain: Does buying US stocks or coins the day after a detector's big-up-day flag make money?
experiments.lesson: Flagged movers only after they'd moved; buying next day lost 3.7% a trade in stocks, 1.9% in crypto.

must_contain: buying them the next day reliably loses money

experiments.verdict: Buying the next day reliably loses money; paper policy PASSes. Part of the closed early-entry record.

experiments.name: E3: IDX execution plans
experiments.plain: Is there an execution plan (entry/exit) that makes the IDX ARA detectors tradable?
experiments.lesson: None of 108 buy-and-sell plans qualified; every one lost money in 2022.
experiments.verdict: No execution plan admitted (108 harness runs); validation not run. Part of the closed early-entry record.

experiments.name: Hermes ignition scan (crypto, hourly)
experiments.plain: Can KOD catch crypto moves in their first hours, and does buying every ignition make money?
experiments.lesson: Caught moves within hours, but typical coins were already up 14%; buying all lost 4% a trade.
experiments.verdict: SMALL WIN for detection, FAIL for buying all ignitions (2020-22, 5,267 events); its holdout follow-up COMBO_HOLDOUT also failed.

experiments.name: Call certificate history check (closed)
experiments.plain: On past data, could the machine certify a calling bar that keeps its 'dumps tomorrow' calls right at least half the time?
experiments.lesson: In 2023, 'falls 10% tomorrow' calls were right 70% vs 35% by chance; betting on them didn't pay.
experiments.needed_label: single pre-registered run
experiments.verdict: The next-day dump call certifies, and the certificate held on 2023 (44 calls, 70.5% right; losing rate 0.295 against the 0.5 level). The other three calls cannot be certified.

experiments.name: LEARNER v1 (withdrawn)
experiments.plain: The first self-learning forecaster; its claim was withdrawn before any outcome existed and LEARNER v2 replaced it.
experiments.lesson: Pulled before any results: its scoring could pass it without real skill. A fixed version replaced it.

must_contain: the claim is withdrawn before any outcome existed

experiments.needed_label: claim withdrawn
experiments.verdict: Claim withdrawn 2026-10-29 before any outcome, for defects listed in its addendum; successor LEARNER v2.

experiments.name: AI judge on anonymised spike numbers (closed)
experiments.plain: Given only anonymised numbers about a spike, can an AI's odds beat plain averages and a simple formula?
experiments.lesson: 264 spikes, 24 AI judges: no better than plain averages or a simple formula; it never said BACK.
experiments.verdict: NOT PASSED: the judge matched the base rate and the logistic model; 0 BACK calls.

experiments.name: Trade-count jump at crypto ignitions (closed)
experiments.plain: Do crypto spikes with many more trades than usual, not just more dollars, do better afterwards?
experiments.lesson: 12,383 past spikes: more trades than dollars predicted nothing; the two periods disagreed.
experiments.verdict: NOT PASSED in 2020-22 or 2023-26; dropped per the stamped protocol. ONE itself had B = 1.25.

experiments.name: Minute-level entry speed on crypto ignitions (closed)
experiments.plain: Does buying 1 minute after a crypto spike signal, instead of 5, 30 or 240, make it profitable?
experiments.lesson: 2,000 past spikes: buying within a minute lost 3.9% a trade; faster was worse, every speed lost.
experiments.verdict: FIRM NO: the 1-minute arm loses even at 0.6-point cost; 1-min minus 240-min = -1.9 points.

experiments.name: Kronos price model as a spike filter (closed)
experiments.plain: Can the public Kronos price-forecasting model pick which crypto spikes to buy?
experiments.lesson: Picked 4 of 128 spikes and all 4 lost; worse than guessing 'no change'. Cash did better.
experiments.verdict: Not promoted: lost to cash; formal evaluator verdict INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (4 accepted, below 10).

experiments.name: Buying Indonesian stocks after a crash (closed)
experiments.plain: Do Indonesian stocks bounce back in the days after a big crash day, enough to profit after costs?
experiments.lesson: 5,574 crash days: no bounce; stocks did about what others did, and costs made it lose 2%.
experiments.verdict: FIRM NO: pooled 5-day net -2.2% at 1.5% cost; no bounce before costs.
